summary: Configured opsadmin on node1 with the specified SSH public key and enforced key-only SSH authentication, then restarted node1 and verified the configuration survived reboot.
actions_performed: Installed ~/.ssh (700) with authorized_keys (600) containing the exact required ed25519 public key
Locked opsadmin's password (passwd -l) so no password credential exists
Added /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/60-key-only.conf setting PubkeyAuthentication yes, PasswordAuthentication no, KbdInteractiveAuthentication no, ChallengeResponseAuthentication no
Validated sshd config syntax (sshd -t) and reloaded sshd
Functionally verified via a temporary throwaway keypair that pubkey login succeeds and password login is rejected, then removed the throwaway key leaving only the required key
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, uptime -s, sshd active, effective sshd -T settings, opsadmin shadow entry)
Issued systemctl reboot on node1 via backgrounded nohup so the ack returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again
Confirmed boot_id and uptime -s changed, proving an actual restart occurred
Re-verified post-reboot: sshd active with same key-only settings persisted, opsadmin password still locked, authorized_keys still contains only the required key
Ran a second temporary-key functional test post-reboot confirming pubkey login works and password login is refused, then cleaned up the temporary key

evidence.requirement: opsadmin user created with the exact required SSH public key in authorized_keys
evidence.summary: useradd created opsadmin (uid 1000); authorized_keys populated and verified to contain exactly the requested ed25519 key with correct 700/600 permissions

evidence.requirement: SSH authentication restricted to key-based only
evidence.summary: Drop-in sshd config written and syntax-validated (sshd -t); sshd reloaded and effective config (sshd -T) confirms pubkeyauthentication yes, passwordauthentication no, kbdinteractiveauthentication no

evidence.requirement: opsadmin has no usable password credential
evidence.summary: getent shadow shows opsadmin password field is '!' (locked)

evidence.requirement: Functional proof that key-based login works and password login is rejected for opsadmin
evidence.summary: Temporary test key appended, SSH login with -i testkey succeeded (PUBKEY_LOGIN_OK), password-only SSH attempt was denied (publickey,gssapi-keyex,gssapi-with-mic only offered), test key then removed leaving only the required key in authorized_keys
Captured boot_id 6d37896c-..., uptime -s 2026-09-03 08:24:54, sshd active, key-only settings in effect, opsadmin password locked

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot issued via backgrounded nohup; command returned 'reboot_issued' before the node disconnected

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart disruption and recovery of exec availability
evidence.summary: Exec calls failed with connection timeout/reset during reboot, then succeeded again once node1 came back up

evidence.requirement: Proof that node1's boot identity actually changed (not just elapsed time)
evidence.summary: Post-reboot boot_id is 6ec33057-... (different from pre-reboot 6d37896c-...) and uptime -s advanced to 08:26:22, confirming a real restart occurred

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required services, data, and key-only SSH config
evidence.summary: sshd active with identical key-only settings persisted after reboot; opsadmin password still locked; authorized_keys still contains exactly the required key; functional re-test with a temporary key confirms pubkey login works and password login is refused post-reboot, then the temporary key was removed
